subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Paediatric solid tumours: neuroblastoma, Wilms, retinoblastoma and beyond

steps.tx: **Neuroblastoma** is the most common extracranial solid tumour of childhood and arises from neural crest cells of the sympathetic nervous system. Most tumours secrete **catecholamines**, so urinary VMA and HVA are elevated. **MYCN amplification** is the major adverse biological marker and demands intensified therapy. Opsoclonus-myoclonus, or dancing eyes-dancing feet syndrome, is a classic paraneoplastic feature.
steps.say: Neuroblastoma is the most common extracranial solid tumour of childhood. It arises from neural crest cells of the sympathetic nervous system. Most tumours secrete catecholamines, so urinary VMA and HVA are raised. MYCN amplification is the major adverse biological marker and calls for intensified therapy. Opsoclonus-myoclonus, also called dancing eyes-dancing feet syndrome, is a classic paraneoplastic feature.

steps.tx: **Wilms tumour** is the most common primary renal malignancy of childhood and usually presents as an asymptomatic abdominal mass. Abdominal pain is the commonest symptom, and hypertension is often seen. Blood pressure typically normalises after nephrectomy. Histology is classed as **favourable** or **anaplastic**; the triphasic pattern of blastema, epithelium and stroma is favourable, while diffuse anaplasia carries roughly 50% recurrence risk.

steps.tx: Genetic markers guide Wilms risk. Alterations in **WT1**, CTNNB1 and WTX occur in roughly one-third of tumours. Loss of **1p and 16q** is an adverse finding even when histology is favourable. **Perilobar nephrogenic rests** in infants under one year carry a raised risk of contralateral disease. Bilateral involvement at diagnosis defines Stage V, while tumour spillage during surgery defines Stage III.

steps.tx: **Retinoblastoma** is the commonest primary intraocular malignancy of childhood and is caused by biallelic loss of the **RB1** gene at 13q14. Leukocoria is the usual presentation. Knudson's two-hit model explains sporadic unilateral disease, which forms about 55% of cases. Examination under anaesthesia remains the gold standard for diagnosis, and MRI is used to assess optic nerve invasion.

Knudson's two-hit model explains sporadic unilateral disease, which forms about 55 percent of cases. Examination under anaesthesia remains the gold standard for diagnosis, and MRI is used to assess optic nerve invasion.

steps.tx: Hereditary **RB1** germline carriers face a lifelong risk of **osteosarcoma** and other non-ocular cancers, and external beam radiotherapy raises secondary malignancy risk substantially. Rarely, **MYCN amplification** drives disease without RB1 mutation. Group C tumours are treated with **chemoreduction**, while group E tumours usually need enucleation. Children of an affected carrier have a 50% inheritance risk.
